As the process servers were well aware, notices posted on apartment doors in the area where these tenants lived were not infrequently removed by children or other tenants before they could have their intended effect.

events.text: The Supreme Court takes the appeal

ACT_5.secondary: Delivering the opinion of the Court

ACT_5.quote: notice reasonably calculated, under all the circumstances, to apprise interested parties of the pendency of the action
ACT_5.attribution: Mullane (1950), the standard applied in Greene v. Lindsey

ACT_5.quote: appellees have been deprived of a significant interest in property — indeed, of the right to continued residence in their homes
A procedure's effect must be judged in the light of its practical application to the affairs of men as they are ordinarily conducted.
ACT_5.attribution: Greene v. Lindsey (1982), stating the test

ACT_5.quote: But whatever the efficacy of posting in many cases, it is clear that, in the circumstances of this case, merely posting notice on an apartment door does not satisfy minimum standards of due process.
ACT_5.attribution: Greene v. Lindsey, 456 U.S. 444 (1982) — the turn

ACT_5.quote: The State's continued exclusive reliance on an ineffective means of service is not notice reasonably calculated to reach those who could easily be informed by other means at hand.

ACT_5.secondary: Deprived of property without the due process of law required by the Fourteenth Amendment

ACT_5.quote: in light of the findings of the courts below, we hold only that posted notice pursuant to section 454.030 is constitutionally inadequate
ACT_5.attribution: Greene v. Lindsey (1982), stating its own limit

lines: IT DID NOT ORDER THE MAIL.

ACT_5.secondary: Joined by the Chief Justice and by Justice Rehnquist

ACT_5.quote: The sole ground for the Court's result is the scant and conflicting testimony of a handful of process servers in Kentucky. On this flimsy basis, the Court confidently overturns the work of the Kentucky Legislature.

ACT_5.quote: It is no secret, after all, that unattended mailboxes are subject to plunder by thieves. Posting, at least, gives assurance that the notice has gotten as far as the tenant's door.
